newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Bank Islam Malaysia to reorganise.
newsitem.headline: Bank Islam Malaysia to reorganise.

text.p: Bank Islam Malaysia Bhd said on Tuesday it plans changes to its group structure including the formation of a new holding company called BIMB Holdings Bhd, a proposed bonus issue of 53.36 million new shares on a two-for-five basis and an exchange of shares of Bank Islam for shares in BIMB Holdings.
In a statement, the bank also said it is proposing the transfer of its investments in seven subsidiaries to the new holding company for 62.9 million ringgit in cash.

BIMB Holdings would also provide 646 million ringgit as a capital injection which would allow the bank to meet the requirements of Tier-one bank status, the highest capital bank standard set by the country's central bank.

Prior to the restructuring, Bank Islam's share capital was 133.41 million ringgit. Its enlarged share capital after the exercise would be 500 million ringgit, which would meet the Tier-one requirement.
Under the proposed restructuring, Bank Islam said it would apply for the delisting of its shares from the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange and for admission of BIMB Holdings' stock in its place.
The plan "is expected to provide the group with more flexibility in future in the raising of funds for the continued growth of the group", as well as boost its competitive edge, the statement said.
Under the proposal, Bank Islam would become a wholly-owned unit of BIMB Holdings and, in turn, the shareholders of the bank would become the shareholders of BIMB Holdings.
